description: Deterministic owner of discovery source identity and behaviour. Source families exist so coverage diversity is measured by real inventory families rather than by nominal site count. This file describes sources only. It never holds candidate preferences, credentials, cookies, account names or private candidate data. Each source also declares which SEARCH families pay off against it and how many result cards are worth inspecting per productive query, so the planner reads those facts rather than a human keeping a prose table in step. Each family also declares a monitoring class, so an omission from a daily plan is a recorded decision rather than an accident.

vocabularies.query_execution_meaning: Whether a requested query is reproducibly EXECUTED, DISPLAYED and VERIFIABLE on this source. `verified` means the rendered page demonstrably reflects the requested query. `unverified` means it could not be confirmed. `ignores_query` means the source was observed returning its unfiltered inventory regardless of the query. Only `verified` may own a mandatory query-specific obligation, because a bucket names a QUERY on an inventory and a source that cannot run the query cannot discharge it.

indeed.notes: QUERYABLE AGAIN as of 2026-09-04, under a PAGE-ONE-ONLY, PACED constraint, after the exclusion's premise was retested and found wrong twice over. FIRST CORRECTION (2026-09-04): the 2026-09-03 claim that every path returned 403 was false. Indeed is reachable server-side: the classic search returns 200 with 16 genuine cards, /m is a 307 to it rather than a 403, the legacy RSS path is 404, /viewjob is 403 and api.indeed.com still does not resolve. SECOND CORRECTION: the blocker is not a request BUDGET, it is PAGINATION. Measured at 45 seconds between requests: a mixed probe reached request 5 and hit a reCAPTCHA on request 6, which was its first &start=10; a page-one-only probe at the same spacing ran 8 for 8 with 16 cards each and no challenge at all. Earlier probes that concluded 'one or two requests' were simply too fast, at 1.5 to 15 seconds. ROBOTS.TXT PERMITS THIS: the User-agent: * group carries Allow: /, disallows neither /jobs nor /viewjob, and explicitly Allows &start=0 through &start=90. The site's stated policy was never the obstacle. OPERATING RULE: one page per query (&start=0 only, never paginate), at least 45 seconds between requests, and STOP AT ONCE on any reCAPTCHA - it is never bypassed, and pacing exists to stay under the limit rather than to get around it. HONEST DEPTH: 16 cards per query is a RELEVANCE-ORDERED SAMPLE of the window, not exhaustive coverage of it, so Indeed is shallow next to LinkedIn (150+/query) or Reed (25/page over hundreds). It is real inventory, not full inventory, and must never be reported as the latter.

adzuna.monitoring_reason: WORKING HYPOTHESIS, not a measurement. Adzuna is an aggregator, so its listings are expected to overlap substantially with Reed, CWJobs, Totaljobs and the employer sites this workspace already searches daily, and an aggregated listing is expected to carry a weaker vacancy identity than the employer or board copy it was drawn from. Neither expectation has been measured here: no production run has yet searched Adzuna, so there is no duplicate rate, no unique-candidate count and no filter-compliance observation in this workspace to appeal to. It is classed `rotating` on that expectation alone, which is why the class carries an empirical review rather than a conclusion. It stays enabled and queryable, and exhaustive mode always reaches it.

adzuna.policy_review_note: Whichever comes first: three successful runs that actually searched it, or the date backstop. If the measured duplicate rate is low or its unique contribution is material, promote it to `daily`. If the hypothesis holds, keep it rotating and record the numbers that justified it. Do not restate the hypothesis as a finding until the numbers exist.

sources.notes: TWO ACCESS PATHS WITH DIFFERENT CAPABILITIES, and the grade above describes the GUEST SEARCH path, which is the one discovery uses. GUEST SEARCH (jobs-guest/jobs/api/seeMoreJobPostings/search) is the dated path: measured 2026-09-03, every card carried a per-item datetime (10 of 10 on each of 26 consecutive pages), f_TPR was honoured per item, and keyword semantics held exactly - 'Python Developer', 'Integration Developer' and 'Junior Backend Developer' returned ZERO overlapping job ids and titles that tracked the query. It paginates with start= in steps of 10 and keeps returning results to start=600, emptying at start=750, so one query reaches several hundred distinct dated vacancies rather than one screen. Deep pages reshuffle slightly, so a small number of ids repeat across pages: deduplicate by job id and never assume start=N holds a stable slice. AUTHENTICATED CARD LIST remains unreliable for freshness and must never be used to prove a window: across three verification searches in run scrape-20260831T083115570281 only 3 of 16 cards carried a readable posted age while 12 were badged Promoted, and the list virtualises so most cards never render. Use it for breadth only, and take dates from the guest path. NEVER pass sortBy=DD on any path. It destroys keyword semantics: 'Python Developer' and 'Integration Developer' returned 17 of 18 identical job ids, and 'Python Django REST Framework' returned Splunk Consultant and Document Review Specialist. Per-vacancy description and posted date: jobs-guest/jobs/api/jobPosting/<jobId>.
sources.guest_search_shard_rationale: The per-query result set is capped PER SEARCH SCOPE, not globally, so the UK-wide query alone reaches roughly half the inventory. Measured 2026-09-03 on 'Python Developer' over a 7-day window, each scope paged to exhaustion: United Kingdom returned 493 unique, while London, Manchester, Birmingham and Cambridge returned 341, 260, 178 and 214, of which 124, 207, 158 and 69 were vacancies the UK-wide query NEVER returned. Union 992 against 493. THESE ARE RECALL WIDENERS, NOT LOCATION FILTERS, and that distinction is not pedantry: measured over 60 cards each, only 18 percent of the Manchester shard's results were actually in Manchester, 8 percent for Birmingham and 10 percent for Cambridge, whose results were mostly London. Only London tracked its own label, at 90 percent. A shard's location can therefore NEVER be used to infer where a vacancy is; take the location from the card. `distance` does not repair this - a London search returned Glasgow and Newcastle at every value from 10 to 100 - so overlap cannot be tuned away and every scope must be deduplicated by job id. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-09-04 on a smaller paced sample (four pages per scope, 14-day window): United Kingdom returned 37 unique ids, and London, Manchester and Cambridge returned 37, 38 and 37, of which 23, 38 and 24 were ids the UK-wide query never returned - Manchester's entire result set was new. Union 101 against 37 for the UK-wide scope alone. The effect is not a stale measurement.
sources.guest_card_fields_note: A guest card carries title, company, location, an ISO datetime, 'Actively Hiring' and sometimes an applicant count. It carries NO salary and NO 'Promoted' badge: measured 2026-09-03, zero promoted markers in the fragment against 12 of 16 on the authenticated card list. So employment_conditions can never be scored from a card, and the promoted-card freshness pathology that affects the authenticated list does not apply to this path.
sources.guest_search_shard_budget_note: inspect_cards_per_query is the budget for the whole QUERY, spent ACROSS the shard list, not per shard. Read it any other way and one query becomes 400 cards times five scopes: eleven bootstrap queries would fetch 22,000 rows against a run ceiling of 8,056, which is 2,200 HTTP requests for a pool the run has already said it will not consider. Spend it BREADTH-FIRST, round robin across the scopes, so every scope is sampled before any one is paged deep. That is also the better trade for recall: the measured value of sharding is that each scope returns vacancies the others never do, so five shallow scopes beat one deep one.
sources.guest_search_window_note: f_TPR takes SECONDS and every one of these is a TRUE per-item filter, verified 2026-09-03: r86400 oldest 1 day, r604800 oldest 6, r1209600 oldest 13 across 120 cards, r2592000 oldest 30 across 120, nothing outside its window in any of them. r1209600 is a real 14-day bucket even though LinkedIn's own UI labels that chip 'Past month'; an earlier note in this workspace trusted the label over the behaviour and wrongly sent the 8-14 day slice elsewhere. Never substitute a wider window: the per-query result set is capped, so r2592000 returned 178 unique of which only 123 were inside 14 days, against r604800's 166 all inside 7.

sources.notes: Aggregator with genuine UK inventory, reachable server-side with the complete browser header set from references/public-sources.md. ONE PAGE PER QUERY, 45s minimum spacing, never paginate, stop instantly on a reCAPTCHA. A card-less or captcha-bearing HTTP 200 is `blocked_captcha`, never `empty`. Resolve promoted and syndicated cards to the employer or original board posting before presenting, since much of Indeed's inventory is republished from ATS feeds this workspace already reads directly.
sources.pagination_note: DO NOT PAGINATE. &start=0 is the only value this source tolerates from an unauthenticated client: measured 2026-09-04, eight consecutive page-one searches at 45s succeeded with 16 cards each, while the first &start=10 request drew an immediate reCAPTCHA. robots.txt allows &start=0..90, so this is a live rate control rather than a permission boundary - the allowance does not mean the server will serve it.
sources.freshness_note: fromage RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-04 and it filters per item: `fromage=14` returned 15 cards, none older than 14 days, every one carrying a readable relative age. Note that ALL 15 were promoted slots (adId set) and they still honoured the window - the opposite of the StepStone PREMIUM pathology, where promoted cards bypass postedwithin entirely. Take the age from each card's own formattedRelativeTime regardless, because trusting the filter and reading the card are not alternatives.

sources.notes: Observed 2026-08-28: the postedwithin filter does not constrain promoted slots. Cards badged PREMIUM or FEATURED appeared under an active Last 24 hours filter showing 1 week ago and 1 month ago. Read every card posted age individually before counting it toward a freshness window.

family_coverage_policy.description: Which inventory families an ordinary run must reach, which rotate, and which are deliberately out of scope. An omission has to be a decision with a reason and a review date. A family quietly missing from every plan looks identical to a family nobody thought about.

classes.rotating: Searched on a documented rolling cycle, not every day.
classes.exhaustive: Reached only by an explicitly requested wide sweep.
classes.excluded: Deliberately not queried. Excluded from every denominator.

family_coverage_policy.notes: Exhaustive mode must reach every enabled, queryable family whose class is not `excluded`; the validator asserts 100 per cent against that denominator. A daily run reaches the daily families plus the rotating families due this cycle, and its plan lists what it omitted and why. Coverage is counted by FAMILY: six sponsor boards inside one family are one family covered, never six, because counting them separately would inflate the number without searching more inventory. A failed or partial run does not advance the cycle, because the families it was supposed to reach were not reached. A rotating family whose own last successful coverage is older than force_due_after_hours becomes due IMMEDIATELY, whatever the cycle position says. Without that override the cycle counts RUNS while the cap counts HOURS, so a workspace run weekly would let a three-run family wait twenty-one days against a fourteen-day cap and lose a week of inventory that nothing could recover. The override is set well below the cap so the pull-forward happens before anything is lost rather than after.
